title: Research note: restored DATA-shear boundaries for PR #521's native BIT query (exact query costs, no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research note with exact verification. No new κ.** The selected certificate, its κ (`51110230636731/31250000000000000`) and `upstream/` are unchanged. All files are new, under `research/native-fusion-restored-shear/`.

For the unipotent ADDRESS permutation `h` of #521 (Karl Appel / @applecrusher, head `a190fdb39f31647fc6f651625353710624627348`), this completes the DATA shear `(x,y,z) -> (x XOR y XOR h(y), y, z)` under three explicit workspace contracts:

| Implementation | Recursive children | Persistent full private rows | Workspace endpoint |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Query the DATA target | 2 | 0 | Every unrelated dirty row preserved |
| Query only private storage with triangular XOR charts | 4 | 1 | Arbitrary private contents restored |
| Owned disposable storage, with paid copy and clear | 1 | 1 | Private row returned to zero |

- **Query minimums.**
  - The two-query minimum is proved in the fixed-`h`, arbitrary-dirty-row XOR model.
  - The four-query minimum holds under the narrower private-only restriction.
  - Neither lower bound covers arbitrary alternative ADDRESS primitives.
- **The one-query implementation** relies on ownership that permits overwriting the private input. It is not a dirty-restoration implementation.
- **Costs.** Complete typed cost recurrences (PROOF.md §6) charge every child, affine event, XOR, copy, clear, routing and inherited tape cost.

**Predecessor work.** Details and pins are in NOTICE.md and SOURCES.json.
- #521 supplies the ADDRESS map, its seven-event lowering and the dirty-module representation. This PR does not review or approve the rest of #521.
- The scalar-projector/group-algebra model comes from #288 (eumemic) and #468 (Ali Romman).
- #83 (Joseph Demarest) scoped the fixed-menu recursion barrier, which this note does not reopen.
- The OpenAI #109 framework interfaces remain premises.

**Open obligations.**
- Place a completed shear inside an actual supplier.
- Authorize its DATA query or disposable storage.
- Price the resulting whole profile.
- Handle arbitrary widths.
- Discharge the inherited all-size and tape interfaces.

No saving is inferred from the local counts.

[Research note](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/613c02b8b4411f991f108dcc1481b3f9100b996f/research/native-fusion-restored-shear/README.md), [proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/613c02b8b4411f991f108dcc1481b3f9100b996f/research/native-fusion-restored-shear/PROOF.md), [attribution](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/613c02b8b4411f991f108dcc1481b3f9100b996f/research/native-fusion-restored-shear/NOTICE.md), [source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/613c02b8b4411f991f108dcc1481b3f9100b996f/research/native-fusion-restored-shear/SOURCES.json), and [completed local claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/613c02b8b4411f991f108dcc1481b3f9100b996f/research/native-fusion-restored-shear/CLAIM.md).

**Overlap.** No pinned coordination issue existed at either check. The pre-submission refresh covered 494 open PRs and found none on #521's restored shear. The nearest are #663, which audits #628's nonlinear dirty restoration, and #665, which prices a width-9 spectral split. Both study different objects.

## Validation

From the repository root (Python 3.10+, standard library only):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/native-fusion-restored-shear/check.py --check
```

Output, re-run on base `66849e1` before submission:

```text
PASS_RESTORED_SHEAR_INTERFACES
60880 signed projector pairs; 4681 native-chart words; 776 BIT basis columns per program; 17 negative controls
Independent full-domain replay: 729 addresses; 2916 basis columns per program; 17496 endpoint/inverse cases
```

- **Finite checks.**
  - Exhaustive enumerations: 60,880 signed projector pairs; all 4,681 native-chart words through length four; dirty BIT columns on full and shorter prime-power orbits.
  - An independently implemented sparse-set replay of all 729 addresses in `(Z/3)^6`.
  - 17 negative controls, all of which the checker rejects.
- **Proof arguments.** The universal claims, the two-query classification and the private-only restriction are written proofs in PROOF.md. They are not inferred from the finite replay.
- **Repository checks.** `make selected-record-check` passes: `PASS selected record, exact kappa, original source inventory and proof supplement: 51110230636731/31250000000000000`. `git diff --check` is clean, and no existing file or `upstream/` byte changes. The replay takes about 1.2 seconds on Linux with Python 3.12.3, standard library only.
- **Not claimed.** This is not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem and not a cold replay of the selected supplier. It is also not a full repository suite, Linux CI or Lean pass.

Sprint: recursive-interfaces track, OS seed 57. The claim and its result update are recorded in CLAIM.md.

Submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6-Astra) wrote the analysis, proof and checker, and Claude Code packaged the submission. No independent human peer review is claimed.
